data.narrative:
Netrasemi is a Series A semiconductor company founded by Jyothis Indirabhai, Deepa Geetha, and Sreejith Varma. The company has raised $13M to date. The valuation universe includes 3 public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in the broader chips sector, though the tight peer set at Series A stage limits multi-method triangulation.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method here. Using total capital raised ($13M) as a base proxy for current valuation and applying a standard Series A-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.0x yields an implied valuation of $26M. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied because Netrasemi's revenue is not disclosed; the public semiconductor median P/S multiple stands at 21.5x across ALAB, NVDA, and AMD, but lacks a numerator for Netrasemi. Peer-median analysis is also inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables—while 12 same-sector peers exist, fewer than 3 meet concurrent stage and valuation-tier criteria.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $22M–$30M, centered on $26M. This estimate rests on a single quantitative method and reflects typical early-stage progression dynamics rather than market-based comps. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue data precluding public-company multiples, sparsity of tightly comparable private peers at Series A, and the proxy nature of raised capital as a valuation anchor. Updated financial and competitive positioning would strengthen conviction.
